title: Beowulf, Prologue
author: Anonymous
source_notes: Old English text from the Klaeber tradition (Cotton Vitellius A. xv manuscript). Translation by Francis B. Gummere, 'The Oldest English Epic', 1910.
reading_notes: The prologue opens with the famous 'Hwæt!' — an exclamation to attention. It names Scyld Scefing, mythic founder of the Danish line, as model for the Spear-Danes' rising glory. The funeral of Scyld closes the prologue and frames the poem that follows.

lines.english: Lo, praise of the prowess of people-kings
lines.gloss: Hwæt = 'Lo, listen!'; We = 'we'; Gardena = 'of the Spear-Danes' (genitive plural); in geardagum = 'in days of yore' (dative plural).

lines.english: of spear-armed Danes, in days long sped,
lines.gloss: þeodcyninga = 'of nation-kings' (genitive plural); þrym = 'glory, might' (accusative singular); gefrunon = 'have heard tell' (perfect plural of frignan).

lines.english: we have heard, and what honor the athelings won!
lines.gloss: hu = 'how'; ða = 'the' (plural); æþelingas = 'nobles, princes' (nominative plural); ellen = 'courage, valor' (accusative); fremedon = 'performed' (past plural).

lines.english: Oft Scyld the Scefing from squadroned foes,
lines.gloss: Oft = 'often'; Scyld Scefing = 'Scyld, son of Scef'; sceaþena = 'of enemies' (genitive plural); þreatum = 'from troops, bands' (dative plural).

lines.english: from many a tribe, the mead-bench tore,
lines.gloss: monegum = 'many' (dative plural); mægþum = 'tribes' (dative plural); meodosetla = 'of mead-seats' (genitive plural); ofteah = 'took away' (past singular of oftēon).

lines.english: awing the earls. Since erst he lay
lines.gloss: egsode = 'terrified' (past singular); eorlas = 'nobles' (accusative plural); syððan = 'since'; ærest = 'first'; wearð = 'became' (past singular of weorðan).

lines.original: feasceaft funden: he þæs frofre gebad,
lines.english: friendless, a foundling, fate repaid him:
lines.gloss: feasceaft = 'destitute' (nominative); funden = 'found' (past participle of findan); he = 'he'; þæs = 'for that' (genitive); frofre = 'consolation' (accusative); gebad = 'awaited, experienced'.

lines.english: for he waxed under welkin, in wealth he throve,
lines.gloss: weox = 'grew' (past singular of weaxan); under = 'under'; wolcnum = 'clouds, sky' (dative plural); weorðmyndum = 'in honors' (dative plural); þah = 'throve' (past of þeon).

lines.original: oð þæt him æghwylc þara ymbsittendra
lines.english: till before him the folk, both far and near,
lines.gloss: oð þæt = 'until that'; him = 'to him' (dative); æghwylc = 'each one' (nominative); þara ymbsittendra = 'of surrounding peoples' (genitive plural).

lines.english: who house by the whale-path, heard his mandate,
lines.gloss: ofer = 'over'; hronrade = 'whale-road, sea' (dative; a kenning); hyran = 'to obey' (infinitive); scolde = 'had to' (past of sculan).

lines.original: gomban gyldan. Þæt wæs god cyning!
lines.english: gave him gifts: a good king he!
lines.gloss: gomban = 'tribute' (accusative); gyldan = 'to pay' (infinitive); Þæt wæs = 'that was'; god cyning = 'good king' (nominative).

lines.english: Afterward a son was born to him,
lines.gloss: Ðæm = 'to him' (dative); eafera = 'heir, son' (nominative); wæs cenned = 'was born' (past passive of cennan); æfter = 'afterward'.

lines.original: geong in geardum, þone god sende
lines.english: young in the courts, whom God sent
lines.gloss: geong = 'young' (nominative); in geardum = 'in the courts' (dative plural); þone = 'whom' (accusative); god = 'God'; sende = 'sent' (past of sendan).

lines.english: as a comfort to the people; He perceived their sore distress
lines.gloss: folce = 'to the people' (dative); to frofre = 'for consolation'; fyrenðearfe = 'dire distress' (accusative); ongeat = 'perceived' (past of ongietan).

lines.english: that they had long endured, lordless,
lines.gloss: þe = 'which' (relative); hie = 'they'; ær = 'previously'; drugon = 'endured' (past plural of dreogan); aldorlease = 'lordless' (plural).

lines.english: for a long while. To them the Lord of Life,
lines.gloss: lange hwile = 'for a long while' (accusative of duration); Him = 'to them' (dative); þæs = 'for that'; liffrea = 'Lord of life' (nominative, a kenning for God).

lines.english: Ruler of glory, granted worldly honor:
lines.gloss: wuldres = 'of glory' (genitive); wealdend = 'ruler' (nominative); woroldare = 'worldly honor' (accusative); forgeaf = 'granted' (past of forgiefan).

lines.english: Beowulf was famous — his fame sprang wide —
lines.gloss: Beowulf = 'Beow/Beowulf' (the Danish prince, not the hero; nominative); wæs = 'was'; breme = 'famous' (nominative); blæd = 'fame' (nominative); wide = 'widely'; sprang = 'sprang' (past of springan).

lines.english: Scyld's heir, in Scandinavian lands.
lines.gloss: Scyldes = 'of Scyld' (genitive); eafera = 'heir' (nominative); Scedelandum = 'Scandinavian lands' (dative plural); in = 'in' (postpositive).

lines.original: Swa sceal geong guma gode gewyrcean,
lines.english: So ought a young man through good deeds work,
lines.gloss: Swa = 'so'; sceal = 'must, ought' (3rd singular of sculan); geong guma = 'young man' (nominative); gode = 'by good' (dative/instrumental); gewyrcean = 'to work, bring about' (infinitive).

lines.english: with splendid gifts while in his father's keeping,
lines.gloss: fromum = 'splendid' (dative plural); feohgiftum = 'money-gifts, treasures' (dative plural); on fæder bearme = 'in the father's bosom / keeping' (prep. + dative).
